parameters.reference:
NOT PINNED — run_corpus_combine.sh passes no --ref, while run_undistort_compose.sh's header says 'on a multi-night compose it must be pinned'. TWO CORRECTIONS TO THAT HEADER, both measured after this record was first written:
(1) THE AUTO-PICK DOES NOT RANK. It takes INDEX 0 — the first member in link order. Measured: reference_member = s_00001 in ALL TEN compose gate records on this rig, at 13/17/22/25/52/77 members. This record previously said the pick 'ranks over the whole member pool', which is wrong in mechanism and wrong about the trigger: appending a night re-bases NOTHING; only a night that sorts FIRST, or a reordering of the session arguments, re-bases anything.
(2) THE ORIENTATION HALF OF THE --ref JUSTIFICATION IS FALSE ON THE SHIPPED ROUTE. Every measurement behind it (docs/dead-ends.md: canvas orientation + channel balance via setref after the 2pass) was taken on the STAR-PAIR route; the shipped route is seqplatesolve, and compose_preflight.py's own docstring says the astrometric route 'lands north-up instead of inheriting whatever orientation the pinned reference member happened to have'. MEASURED on the shipped products: composites sit at north-angle -0.44 deg (corpus) and +0.32 deg (night), while members sit at -164.77, +164.35 and -176.57 deg. The composite inherits NO member's orientation.
The BALANCE half is not refuted but is UNVERIFIED on this route, and the code gives a reason to doubt it: `setref s N` applies to the `s` sequence while -norm=addscale runs in a SEPARATE siril invocation over the `r_s` sequence seqapplyreg created. A one-knob probe is running.
CONSEQUENCE FOR ANY A/B: this product is NOT a --ref control. It was built with no --ref, so bit-identity against it can only be achieved by reproducing the auto-pick — the very behaviour a derivation would replace. It IS a valid control for --central (0.5) and --max-stars (default 200), whose values this record states.

solve.DEFECT_FOUND_IN_finish_render: finish_render.sh line 143 hardcodes --max-stars=400 and does not expose it. On this Milky-Way field that produced logodds 63 — FLOOR-CLASS, below the confident-match floor of 100 — where the default 200 gives 106. solve_field.py's own docstring gives the mechanism: brightest-first selection clusters stars in the galactic band, so 400 over-constrains the order-3 SIP fit and leaves the corners extrapolating. The rendered surface above was produced by running finish_render's stages MANUALLY with max-stars=200; the shipped script would still emit a floor-class solve. NOT FIXED — build-path change, owner's call.
solve.also: run_corpus_combine.sh never passes --central either, though finish_render accepts it and a framing=max union's coverage seams false-detect. Two blind attempts burned 89 minutes before --central solved it in 6 seconds.
